chunks: Al-Mudhaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Mudhaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi narrated that Ja'far ibn Mas'ood narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever fasts one day in Sha'ban seeking the reward of Allah, he will enter Paradise.

And whoever seeks forgiveness from Allah seventy times each day in Sha'ban, Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment in the company of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
And a special favor/grace becomes obligatory for him from Allah.
And whoever gives charity in Sha'ban, even if it is half of a date, Allah will forbid his body from the Fire.
And whoever fasts three days in Sha'ban and connects them with the fasting of the month of Ramadan, Allah will record for him the fasting of two consecutive months.

key_terms.الْكَرَمَةُ: Generosity/Favor (a specific divine gift or honor)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and rewards of fasting and charity in the month of Sha'ban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the spiritual potency of Sha'ban as a preparatory month for Ramadan, linking specific acts like fasting, istighfar, and charity to tangible eschatological rewards. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on voluntary worship (nafl) as a means to attain divine grace (karama) and intercession, reinforcing the continuity between the 'Month of Forgiveness' and the 'Month of Patience'.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-6 Al-Mudhaffar ibn Ja’far Al-Mudhaffar al-Alawi As-Samarqandi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas’ood quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fadhdhal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Waleed, on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Hilal, “I heard Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s) say, ‘Whoever fasts on one of the days in the (Arabic) month of Sha’ban for the sake of God or repents seventy times on one of the days in the (Arabic) month of Sha’ban will be resurrected by the Honorable the Exalted God along with the nation of God’s Prophet (s). He will deserve to receive an honor from God. God will forbid the Fire from touching the corpse of whoever gives some charity in the (Arabic) month of Sha’ban, even if it be as much as half of a date. God will record two consecutive months of fasting for whoever fasts for three days in the (Arabic) month of Sha’ban and continues on fasting for the (Arabic) month of Ramadhan.’”
